The bearer automatically fails all Special Saves, 
regardless of whether Using the Shield or not.

Aegis(4+), and the model’s Armour is always 3.

Attacks with Armour Penetration 3 or less can never

One use only. Duration: End of Combat. 
May be activated when Choosing Equipment and Abilities. 
 The bearer’s unit gains Flaming Attacks

The bearer’s unit may reroll failed Panic Tests. 
If the Battle Standard Bearer or the General is part of the bearer’s unit, it automatically passes Panic Tests instead.

One use only. Duration: End of Turn. 
May be activated at the start of any Phase. 
 The bearer’s unit gains Hard Target (2)

One use only. Duration: End of Combat. 
May be activated when Choosing Equipment and Abilities: 
 Rank-and-File models in the bearer’s unit gain +1 AP.

rules.name: Vorpal Binding

Successful Armour Saves, Regeneration Saves and Aegis Saves against 
attacks made with Vorpal Binding must be rerolled.

rules.name: Crown of the Wizard King
rules.description:
During Pre-game Selections, randomise a Magic Path (from all ten Paths in this book). 
The wearer is a Wizard Apprentice using the 
 randomised Path, and may not Swap any spells. 
The bearer cannot take any Magic Items nor any other upgrades that are restricted to Wizards (or any types of Wizards).

rules.description:
Stand Behind. 
 The wearer’s model loses Stubborn, Bodyguard, cannot gain either in any way, and is never considered to fulfil the criteria of Bodyguard.
 In addition, the model cannot make any Supporting Attacks.

Channel (1).

Rage. 
 All Melee Attacks made by or against the wearer gain +1 to hit.

rules.name: Obsidian Rock
rules.description: Magic Resistance (2).

rules.name: Rod of Battle
rules.description:
The bearer can cast a unique Bound Spell:
Rod of Battle: Casting Value (4+)
Type: Range 18", Augment. Duration: One Turn.
Effect:
The target’s Standard Melee Attacks gain +1 to hit.

rules.name: Binding Scroll
rules.description:
One use only. Duration: One Phase 
Can be activated during the opponent’s Siphon the Veil (Magic Phase, step 2). 
 When activated, choose a Caster and select one of their spells (Bound or Learned): the chosen Caster cannot voluntarily cast the selected instance of this spell. 
E.g. if a caster has the same spell more than one time, only a single instance cannot be cast, and this has no effect on Magical Mishap

rules.name: Scroll of a Free Mind
rules.description:
One use only. Duration: Permanent
Can be activated in a friendly Magic Phase before drawing a Flux card the bearer loses all its learned spells from its selected path granted by Wizard Apprentice, Wizard Adept or Wizard Master. Hereditary and Spells granted by other sources are unaffected. 

The bearer gains the same number of spells from a single other path available to the bearer during list creation.
The spells are gained starting from the first spell of the path and towards the last spell of the path. 
This does not change the bearer’s Path Selection.

Note: This means a single Wizard can gain the same spell twice, yet still not cast the same spell multiple times. 
 Example: a Vampire Wizard Adept with Gates of the Netherworld that selected #1, and #3 from Occultism and swapped to Arise! during List Creation selects Evocation with Scroll of the Free Mind, now knows Whispers of the Veil twice. Danse Macabre, and Arise!.

rules.name: Potion of Power Preservation
rules.description:
One use only. Duration: Instant.
May be used immediately when a Casting Roll or Dispel Roll fails, due to not rolling high enough: do not discard the Magic Dice used in this unsuccessful attempt.

rules.name: Dragon's Brew
rules.description:
One use only. Duration: End of Turn

 Breath Attack(Str 4, AP 1, Flaming Attacks, Stand and Shoot).

rules.name: Potion of Swiftness
rules.description:
One use only. Duration: Round of Combat.
+3 Agi.

rules.name: Scroll of Draining
rules.description:
One use only. Duration: Instant.
May be activated in the opponent’s Magic Phase, immediately after Excess Magic: the opponent immediately discards 1 Magic Dice.

rules.name: Potion of Healing
rules.description:
One use only. Duration: Instant.
The bearer’s model Recovers 1 HP.

rules.name: Scroll of Power
rules.description:
One use only. Duration: Instant.
May be used immediately after a Casting Roll: the bearer may add one additional free Magic Dice to this Casting Roll (the limit of 5 Magic Dice still applies).

rules.name: Spell Scroll
rules.description:
One use only. Duration: One Phase

May be activated at any time during your Magic Phase. The bearer knows the spell indicated in brackets (X) in addition to its other spells, 
(if the bearer already knows the spell, this has no effect).

sharedRules.name: How to Use this Document
sharedRules.description: This document describes the different Paths of Magic and Special Items available for The 9th Age: Fantasy Battles and as such is to be used in conjunction with the main Rulebook. For convenience, we repeated the main rules related to spells and Magic Items from the Rulebook in the corresponding sections below, along with the information needed to read the Paths.

sharedRules.name: Paths of Magic
sharedRules.description: Spells are cast during the Magic Phase. Most spells belong to a specific Path of Magic.

sharedRules.name: Faction Specific Spells
sharedRules.description: Each Faction has some unique spells to cast.

sharedRules.name: Spell Name
sharedRules.description: Use the spell’s name to indicate which spell you want to cast.

sharedRules.name: Casting Value
sharedRules.description: The Casting Value (CV) is the minimum number you need to roll with Magic Dice to successfully cast the spell.

sharedRules.name: Spell Type
sharedRules.description:
The Spell Type specifies how the target of the spell is chosen. A spell can have one or more of the following spell Types: 
 • Augment: can only target friendly units, (or friendly models within units if Focused). 
 • Aura: targets all eligible targets. 
 For example, a spell with Augment, Aura, and Range 12" targets all friendly units within 12" of the Caster. 
 • Caster: can only target the model casting the spell. 
 • Damage: can only target units not Engaged in Combat. 
 When the origin of the damage direction is relevant, it is determined by the point from which the damage range is measured. E.g For Wrath of God the damage direction would be measured from the Wrath of God marker. 
 • Focused: can only target single models, including Attachable Models inside units. If a model consisting of multiple model parts is targeted, only one part can be chosen. 
 • Ground: the spell targets a point on the Battlefield rather than units or models. 
 • Hex: can only target enemy units, (enemy models within units if Focused). 
 • Missile: can only target units within the Caster’s Line of Sight, and cannot be cast if the Caster is Engaged in Combat. When casting a spell with Type: Missile, check which is the Target Facing (see Shooting Phase chapter). 
 • Range X": the spell has a maximum casting range. Targets must be within X" of the Caster. 
 • Universal: the spell can target both friendly and enemy units (or models within units if Focused).

sharedRules.name: Replicable
sharedRules.description:
Multiple attempts at casting a Replicable spell can be made in the same Magic Phase without suffering the normal -3 modifier to the Casting Roll (or -1 in the case of Bound Spells). 
 Note that the spell still can not be attempted multiple times to be cast by the same Wizard.

sharedRules.name: Duration
sharedRules.description: All spells have a Duration, which follows the same rule as described under Duration of Effects (see the Definitions and Terminology chapter).

sharedRules.name: Effect
sharedRules.description: The effect of a spell describes what happens to the target when the spell is successfully cast.

sharedRules.name: Larger Bases
sharedRules.description:
In an army with Larger Bases, models can use different Base Sizes from those listed in their unit entries. This is to allow people with models on slightly larger bases to play The 9th Age. 
 Each unit using this option must have the new base size noted on the Army List, and all models in a unit must have the same base size. 
 The Base Sizes must be: 
 • 100% -- 125% of the original width 
 • 100% -- 150% of the original depth 
 • Both width and depth must be divisible by 5mm 
 In addition, Attachable models with increased Base Sizes can only join Units with the same percentage increase(s) to their Base Sizes. 
 If the models with increased Base Size make up 25% or less of the total model count, the army suffers a penalty of -200 Victory Points at the end of the game (to a minimum of 0). Armies with more than 25% (or none at all) do not suffer this penalty.
 Note: The purpose of this rule is to allow people to use models from different game systems to test out T9A or to use their particularly imposing models legally.

sharedRules.name: Properties of
sharedRules.description:
The following terms are common keywords used to describe Magic Items: 
 • Category: each Magic Item belongs to a single Category, listed below. No model or unit can select more than one Magic Item from each Category. 
 • Dominant: a model can only have one Dominant Magic Item, no matter its Category. 
 • Legendary: all Magic Items are Legendary, unless stated otherwise.

sharedRules.name: Who is affected ?
sharedRules.description:
Unless specifically mentioned otherwise: 
 • Global and Defensive Characteristic modifiers are applied only to the model part taking the Magic Item (and not to other model parts such as mounts)*. 
 • Model Rules that are not Attack Attributes are applied to the combined model as a whole. 
 • Offensive Characteristic modifiers and Attack Attributes are applied only to the model part bearing or wearing the item. 
 • Rules and modifiers from a Weapon Enchantment are only applied to the Standard Melee Attacks made with the Enchanted Weapon. 
 
 Exceptions to the above may be noted in the item’s description, using terminology such as: 
 • The wielder, wearer, bearer - these terms mean the same thing for rules purposes and refer to the model part the Magic Item was bought for, and therefore generally do not affect mounts. 
 • The wielder’s model, wearer’s model, bearer’s model - these terms refer to all model parts of the model the Magic Item was bought for, including their mounts. 
 • The wielder’s unit, wearer’s unit, bearer’s unit - these terms refer to all model parts in the same unit as the model the Magic Item was bought for, including mounts and the model itself. 
 *Characters on mounts with fixed Global or Defensive Characteristics values (i.e. any value that is not C or C+X) do not benefit from modifiers to those Characteristics. 
 See the Character Mounts section of the Characters chapter for examples of interactions with mounts.

sharedRules.name: List of Common and Shared
sharedRules.description: Magic Items fall into one of the following categories.

sharedRules.name: Weapon Enchantments
sharedRules.description:
Weapon Enchantments are upgrades that enhance weapons. A weapon on which a Weapon Enchantment is applied becomes an Enchanted Weapon. The Army List must indicate which weapon that the model is equipped with is an Enchanted Weapon (reminder: models are equipped with a Hand Weapon by default). 
 Each Weapon Enchantment can only enchant particular weapon types (e.g. Great Weapon) or a category of weapons (e.g. Melee Weapon).
 The following rules apply to all Enchanted Weapons, unless specifically mentioned otherwise: 
 • If a model is equipped with an Enchanted Weapon it must use it in Combat whenever possible. 
 • All attacks made with the Enchanted Weapon gain Magical Attacks. 
 • The Enchanted Weapon follows the rules for both its original weapon type and the Weapon Enchantment. 
 • See the rules for weapons (Model Rules) for details on when to apply modifiers and additional rules.

sharedRules.name: Armour Enchantments
sharedRules.description:
These upgrades apply to pieces of armour carried by a model, and can in general be taken by any model. That model is then considered as wearing an Enchanted Armour.
 If an Armour Enchantment is restricted to models with a minimum Armour value, for this purpose only consider the model’s part unmodified base Armour value (excluding mounts), the number written on its profile in the Army Book.
 The following rules apply to all Armour Enchantments, unless specifically mentioned otherwise: 
 • Characteristics modifiers, Model Rules, and all other rules associated with Armour Enchantments are generally only applied to the model part wearing the Enchanted Armour, and do not affect other model parts such as mounts. This includes modifiers to Global and Defensive Characteristics. 
 However, note that certain Model Rules, particularly Model Rules that are neither an Attack Attribute nor a weapon, are always applied to the combined model (and not only to individual model parts). 
 For example the Basalt Infusion provides +1 Arm and Aegis. +1 Arm is a Characteristic modifier, and is thus only applied to the Character wearing the Enchanted Armour. 
 If this Character rides a mount that has its own Armour value, the Armour modifier from Basalt Infusion has no effect on the combined model. 
 However, Aegis is a Global Model Rule, which means it is not applied to an individual model part, but to the whole combined model.

sharedRules.name: Shield Enchantments
sharedRules.description:
Shield Enchantments are upgrades that apply to Shields. An Enchanted Shield follows the rules for both the original Shield and the Shield Enchantment.
 The following rules apply to all Shield Enchantments, unless specifically mentioned otherwise: 
 • The effect of a Shield Enchantment only applies when the bearer of the Enchanted Shield is Using a Shield (remember that a model part cannot use a Shield to protect against Melee Attacks when it is using a Two-Handed weapon in Combat). 
 • Characteristic modifiers, Model Rules, and all other rules associated with Shield Enchantments follow the same rules as for Armour Enchantments.

sharedRules.name: Artefacts
sharedRules.description: Artefacts are unique and powerful items that can have various effects. No additional rules apply to Artefacts.

sharedRules.name: Potions and Scrolls
sharedRules.description:
Potions and Scrolls are Magic Items that provide temporary effects when consumed by a model.
 The following rules apply to all Potions and Scrolls, unless specifically mentioned otherwise: 
 • Potions and Scrolls can be activated at the start of any phase, or during Combat Choices in a Round of Combat. 
 • Their effects (including Characteristic modifiers and Attack Attributes) are only applied to the model part taking the Magic Item, and do not affect other model parts such as mounts.

sharedRules.name: Banner Enchantments
sharedRules.description: Banner Enchantments are upgrades for Battle Standard Bearer and units containing a Standard Bearer, assuming these units have access to Magic Items (as indicated in their unit entry).
